segments.en: Letter 24 is a brief but important letter centered on the commandment of maaser — tithing one's income for charity. Rabbi Shimshon's counsel to his son Nosson: give the tenth even when your income seems scarce, for this is the teaching of the Sages, and the books of the Rebbe confirm that maaser is a propitious segulah for ample livelihood. He also cites Likutay Moharan Part 2 on the teaching of "G-d Almighty give you mercy" — one should not demand good according to one's own logic, but simply trust that all is for the good.

Letter 25 is very brief — a fragment — reporting that there is nothing new regarding livelihood, that G-d performs great miracles, but that great mercy is still needed. Pure trust is the only counsel.

Letter 26 contains two major teachings and one deeply personal account. Teaching 1: the remedy for the battle of thought (milchemes hamachshavah) is the book Alim LiTrufah — read its letters about R' Yitzchak and Reb Nosson's exchange on overcoming intrusive thoughts. Teaching 2: Likutay Moharan 35 — commerce conducted in faith is equivalent to the Temple sacrifices and incense. Personal account: Rabbi Shimshon's son Pinchas was summoned before the Soviet military authorities — a life-threatening danger. Rabbi Shimshon's response was prayer and a small act of charity, following the Talmudic principle of praying before trouble. G-d saved Pinchas for one year.

Letter 27 recommends the Likutay Aitzos of R' Nachman of Tcherin as an abridgment of all of Likutay Halachos. Then a pointed observation: those who seek specifically the hard-to-find volumes of Likutay Halachos — while ignoring the available ones — are being manipulated by the evil inclination. The accessible Orach Chaim Part 1, studied truly, is sufficient to make a person a complete Tzadik.

Letter 28 urges Nosson to establish a daily fixed study in the Likutay Aitzos with the Hebrew-Yiddish commentary that Rabbi Shimshon himself is preparing — studying with patience and great attention, both the original and the commentary. This is the foundation of all true Judaism.

Letter 29 addresses financial hardship with the famous Rebbe Nachman teaching transmitted through Reb Nosson: when Reb Nosson spoke to the Rebbe about livelihood, the Rebbe replied with two words: "Only trust." And a second remarkable teaching: the Rebbe's response to a man who apologized for having inadequate housing for divine service — "If G-d knew your rectification depended on better lodgings, He would have given them to you."

Letter 30 is a fragment urging his son to begin the printing of the Likutay Aitzos with Hebrew-Yiddish commentary — stressing that such a printing has never existed in the world, making it a commandment of incomparable greatness.

Letter 31 reveals the full picture of Rabbi Shimshon's life project in his final years: a sick man, living perpetually by miracles, yet pouring all his strength — and beyond his strength — into preparing the Likutay Aitzos with a Yiddish commentary, driven by a deep inner feeling of its necessity for the revelation of the Rebbe's daas in the world.
